name: Saint Louis
history: Louis IX became King of France at twelve and reigned for over forty years as a just and devout king. He fed the poor at his own table, built the Sainte-Chapelle to house the Crown of Thorns, was loved for his fairness, and twice went on crusade. He died near Tunis in 1270 and was canonised in 1297.
life: Louis was crowned in 1226, and his mother, Blanche of Castile, ruled for him until he came of age. She told him she would rather see him dead than guilty of a mortal sin, and he never forgot it. He married Margaret of Provence, and they had eleven children. His friend and biographer Jean de Joinville describes him sitting under an oak at Vincennes to hear the complaints of anyone who came. He reformed the royal courts, forbade judicial duels, founded hospitals including the Quinze-Vingts for the blind, and served the poor with his own hands. In 1239 he acquired the Crown of Thorns and built the Sainte-Chapelle in Paris for it. He led a crusade to Egypt in 1248, was captured and ransomed, and stayed four years in the Holy Land. On a second crusade in 1270 he fell sick at Tunis and died, praying for his people.
prayerTo: Saint Louis, king and servant of the poor, you ruled justly and kept your soul free of sin amid wealth and power. Pray for all who govern and judge, for husbands and fathers, and for me, that I may use whatever authority I have for the good of others and the glory of God. Amen.
penance: Serve someone poorer than you with your own hands today, perhaps by helping at a soup kitchen or bringing a meal to a neighbour.
meditation: Louis wrote to his son that he should have a tender heart for the poor and the suffering. Whose need have you been too busy to notice?
prayer: O God, Who transported Your blessed Confessor Louis from an earthly throne to the glory of the heavenly kingdom, by his merits and intercession we beseech You to make us of the company of the King of kings, Jesus Christ Your Son. Who livest and reignest with God the Father…
prayerSource: Collect of the day, Roman Missal of 1962
